variants.direction: L06: a simple eight-sided fuselage, widest just behind the front collar, tapering through a shallow waist toward a compact blunt stern. Its flanks are two large planes meeting along one clean longitudinal change of angle. Keep the upper roof broad enough for the two longitudinal doors. Each wing consists of three straight-edged trapezoidal sectors forming a broad stepped fan, with clipped tips and no concave scallops. A single triangular relief at each root separates the front shoulder from the fan attachment. Integrate the two stacked engine openings into the end of the same fuselage. No rear spoiler or dorsal fin. This is one faceted body and its fan wings, with a recognizably different section from the original. Label "L06".
variants.prompt:
Create a SIMPLE GEOMETRIC SHAPE STUDY for a pirate refit of Freelancer's Liberty elite fighter. This is an early hull design study: clear solid volumes, large planar faces, functional joints. Use the source's low-complexity geometric language.

Image 1 is the ORIGINAL unmodified ship in neutral materials. Use its cockpit scale, broad three-leaf fan wings, body depth, three thin neck collar plates, and especially its UPPER-LEFT CAMERA ANGLE as the presentation reference.
Image 2 is an enlarged exact cockpit reference. Preserve its complete rounded capsule, surrounding shell, every actual blue-grey glass pane and the native narrow window frames. The cockpit projects ahead of the collar and itself forms the nose. Keep this geometry and scale. Render its shell grey like the rest of the shape study; do not import its surface texture decoration.

Design the new hull using a FEW SIMPLE CONNECTED SOLIDS. The main fuselage is one coherent volume with a deliberate change of section. Each wing is exactly three broad flat solid polygonal leaves, with straight outlines and clear overlap seams. Leave a compact real attachment to the hull. The stern is one simple housing for two vertically stacked aft-facing engines. Give the body full depth and an angular belly, retaining the original ship's height; do not squash it into a flat aircraft. Deployed span stays similar to total ship length.

Show only primary shape and necessary moving-part divisions. NO decorative ribs, edge framing, stepped armor stacks, extra fins, layered rear crests, sculptural towers, ornamental grilles, radiating engraved lines, scalloped bat wings, pipes, scaffolding, rivets, little hatches, repeated inset panels, weathering or surface texture noise. Faces should be largely uninterrupted. A few deliberate contour cuts and one darker replacement section can communicate the pirate alteration.

Preserve the original three-leaf folding topology: leaves fan outward in inclined planes in flight and nest inward/back for docking. Two narrow long cargo doors sit side by side on the central roof, with a FRONT-TO-BACK seam. They open outward/up along their outer long edges, so keep their sweep unobstructed. Exactly two engines on one vertical centerline, upper larger; in TOP the upper hides the lower. Engines are simple closed polygonal/cylindrical forms, not elaborate turbine stacks.

PRESENTATION IS CRITICAL: neutral light-grey clay hull, blue-grey cockpit glazing, very few darker mechanical faces, soft even light on clean off-white. Precise product-design drawing with sharp planar transitions.
A landscape sheet with THREE LARGE READABLE VIEWS. Left 60% of sheet: upper panel a near-ORTHOGRAPHIC SIDE THREE-QUARTER view, nose LEFT, matching image 1 upper-left camera. Camera mostly perpendicular to the ship's long axis, only slightly toward the nose, around 20 degrees above it. Long-lens appearance, almost no perspective convergence. The whole side contour, hull depth and wing attachment must be legible. Do NOT use a dramatic nose-on view, a large foreground cockpit or an overhead perspective. Lower-left panel: strict SIDE elevation, nose LEFT, same overall length. Right 40% of sheet: a large strict TOP view, nose UP, so its full deployed span and body proportions are obvious. Leave clear space between the three ships. All views depict the same design, in deployed flight.
Text only: concept code specified below, "SIDE", "TOP".

L06: a simple eight-sided fuselage, widest just behind the front collar, tapering through a shallow waist toward a compact blunt stern. Its flanks are two large planes meeting along one clean longitudinal change of angle. Keep the upper roof broad enough for the two longitudinal doors. Each wing consists of three straight-edged trapezoidal sectors forming a broad stepped fan, with clipped tips and no concave scallops. A single triangular relief at each root separates the front shoulder from the fan attachment. Integrate the two stacked engine openings into the end of the same fuselage. No rear spoiler or dorsal fin. This is one faceted body and its fan wings, with a recognizably different section from the original. Label "L06".

variants.direction: L07: a compact wedge-shaped fuselage with a narrow front neck, two broad sloping side faces and a taller squared-off stern. The upper silhouette rises gently toward the rear as ONE continuous sloped volume, with no added rear fins or secondary terraces. The lower hull has one decisive diagonal cut rising into the stern. Put the longitudinal roof doors on the clear central flat portion ahead of that rise. Attach three simple broad polygonal fan leaves on each side through one short solid angular shoulder; the first leaf reaches farther forward and the following two step backward, all with straight sharp edges. Make the root position and the wedge profile visibly different from L06. The two stacked engines remain compact and integrated in the rear face. No disconnected pods, rear wings, ornamental ribs or huge roof crest. Label "L07".
